1: of Hebrew origin; the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only (from its use as a numeral) the first: --Alpha. Often used (usually , before a vowel) also in composition (as a contraction from ἄνευ) in the sense of privation; so, in many words, beginning with this letter; occasionally in the sense of union (as a contraction of ἅμα).
10: of Hebrew origin (אֲבִיהוּד); Abihud, an Israelite:--Abiud.
11: of Hebrew origin (אַבְרָהָם); Abraham, the Hebrew patriarch:--Abraham. (In Acts 7:16 the text should probably read Jacob.)
12: from Α (as a negative particle) and a variation of βυθός; depthless, i.e. (specially) (infernal) "abyss":--deep, (bottomless) pit.
13: of Hebrew origin (compare חָגָב); Agabus, an Israelite:--Agabus.
14: from ἀγαθός and ἔργον; to work good:--do good.
15: from ἀγαθοποιός; to be a well-doer (as a favor or a duty):--(when) do good (well).
17: from ἀγαθός and ποιέω; a well-doer, i.e. virtuous:--them that do well.
18: a primary word; "good" (in any sense, often as noun):--benefit, good(-s, things), well. Compare καλός.
19: from ἀγαθός; goodness, i.e. virtue or beneficence:--goodness.
2: of Hebrew origin (אַהֲרוֹן); Aaron, the brother of Moses:--Aaron.
20: from ἀγαλλιάω; exultation; specially, welcome:--gladness, (exceeding) joy.
21: from agan (much) and ἅλλομαι; properly, to jump for joy, i.e. exult:--be (exceeding) glad, with exceeding joy, rejoice (greatly).
22: from Α (as a negative particle) and γάμος; unmarried:--unmarried.
23: from (much) and (grief; akin to the base of ἀγκάλη); to be greatly afflicted, i.e. (figuratively) indignant:--be much (sore) displeased, have (be moved with, with) indignation.
25: perhaps from (much) (or compare עֲגַב); to love (in a social or moral sense):--(be-)love(-ed). Compare φιλέω.
26: from ἀγαπάω; love, i.e. affection or benevolence; specially (plural) a love-feast:--(feast of) charity(-ably), dear, love.
27: from ἀγαπάω; beloved:--(dearly, well) beloved, dear.
28: of Hebrew origin (הָגָר); Hagar, the concubine of Abraham:--Hagar.
29: of foreign origin (compare אִגְּרָא); properly, to be a courier, i.e. (by implication) to press into public service:--compel (to go).
3: of Hebrew origin (אֲבַדּוֹן); a destroying angel:--Abaddon.
30: from (a pail, perhaps as bent; compare the base of ἀγκάλη); a receptacle:--vessel.
31: from ἄγγελος; an announcement, i.e. (by implication) precept:--message.
32: from (probably derived from ἄγω; compare ἀγέλη) (to bring tidings); a messenger; especially an "angel"; by implication, a pastor:--angel, messenger.
33: imperative of ἄγω; properly, lead, i.e. come on:--go to.
35: from Α (as negative particle) and γενεαλογέω; unregistered as to birth:--without descent.
36: from Α (as negative particle) and γένος; properly, without kin, i.e. (of unknown descent, and by implication) ignoble:--base things.
37: from ἅγιος; to make holy, i.e. (ceremonially) purify or consecrate; (mentally) to venerate:--hallow, be holy, sanctify.
38: from ἁγιάζω; properly, purification, i.e. (the state) purity; concretely (by Hebraism) a purifier:--holiness, sanctification.
39: neuter of ἅγιος; a sacred thing (i.e. spot):--holiest (of all), holy place, sanctuary.
4: from Α (as a negative particle) and βάρος; weightless, i.e. (figuratively) not burdensome:--from being burdensome.
40: from (an awful thing) (compare ἁγνός, θάλπω); sacred (physically, pure, morally blameless or religious, ceremonially, consecrated):--(most) holy (one, thing), saint.
41: from ἅγιος; sanctity (i.e. properly, the state):--holiness.
42: from ἅγιος; sacredness (i.e. properly, the quality):--holiness.
44: from the same as ἀγκάλη; a hook (as bent):--hook.
45: from the same as ἀγκάλη; an "anchor" (as crooked):--anchor.
46: from Α (as a negative particle) and the same as γναφεύς; properly, unfulled, i.e. (by implication) new (cloth):--new.
47: from ἁγνός; cleanliness (the quality), i.e. (specially) chastity:--purity.
48: from ἁγνός; to make clean, i.e. (figuratively) sanctify (ceremonially or morally):--purify (self).
49: from ἁγνίζω; a cleansing (the act), i.e. (ceremonially) lustration:--purification.
5: of Chaldee origin (אַב); father as a vocative:--Abba.
50: from Α (as a negative particle) and νοιέω; not to know (through lack of information or intelligence); by implication, to ignore (through disinclination):--(be) ignorant(-ly), not know, not understand, unknown.
51: from ἀγνοέω; a thing ignored, i.e. shortcoming:--error.
53: from the same as ἅγιος; properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent, modest, perfect:--chaste, clean, pure.
54: from ἁγνός; cleanness (the state), i.e. (figuratively) blamelessness:--pureness.
55: adverb from ἁγνός; purely, i.e. honestly:--sincerely.
56: from Α (as negative particle) and γνῶσις; ignorance (properly, the state):--ignorance, not the knowledge.
57: from Α (as negative particle) and γνωστός; unknown:--unknown.
58: from (to gather; probably akin to ἐγείρω); properly, the town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or thoroughfare:--market(-place), street.
59: from ἀγορά; properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase; specially, to redeem:--buy, redeem.
6: of Hebrew origin (הֶבֶל); Abel, the son of Adam:--Abel.
60: from ἀγορά; relating to the market-place, i.e. forensic (times); by implication, vulgar:--baser sort, low.
61: from ἄγω; (abstractly) a catching (of fish); also (concretely) a haul (of fish):--draught.
62: from Α (as negative particle) and γράμμα; unlettered, i.e. illiterate:--unlearned.
63: from ἀγρός and αὐλέω (in the sense of αὐλή); to camp out:--abide in the field.
64: from ἄγρα; to hunt, i.e. (figuratively) to entrap:--catch.
65: from ἄγριος and ἐλαία; an oleaster:--olive tree (which is) wild.
66: from ἀγρός; wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or figuratively (fierce):--wild, raging.
67: apparently from ἄγριος and ἵππος; wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the Herods:--Agrippa.
68: from ἄγω; a field (as a drive for cattle); genitive case, the country; specially, a farm, i.e. hamlet:--country, farm, piece of ground, land.
69: ultimately from Α (as negative particle) and ὕπνος; to be sleepless, i.e. keep awake:--watch.
7: of Hebrew origin (אֲבִיָּה); Abijah, the name of two Israelites:--Abia.
70: from ἀγρυπνέω; sleeplessness, i.e. a keeping awake:--watch.
71: a primary verb; properly, to lead; by implication, to bring, drive, (reflexively) go, (specially) pass (time), or (figuratively) induce:--be, bring (forth), carry, (let) go, keep, lead away, be open.
72: reduplicated from ἄγω; a bringing up, i.e. mode of living:--manner of life.
73: from ἄγω; properly, a place of assembly (as if led), i.e. (by implication) a contest (held there); figuratively, an effort or anxiety:--conflict, contention, fight, race.
74: from ἀγών; a struggle (properly, the state), i.e. (figuratively) anguish:--agony.
75: from ἀγών; to struggle, literally (to compete for a prize), figuratively (to contend with an adversary), or genitive case (to endeavor to accomplish something):--fight, labor fervently, strive.
76: of Hebrew origin (אָדָם); Adam, the first man; typically (of Jesus) man (as his representative):--Adam.
77: from Α (as negative particle); and δαπάνη; costless, i.e. gratuitous:--without expense.
78: probably of Hebrew origin (compare עֲדִי); Addi, an Israelite:--Addi.
79: feminine of ἀδελφός; a sister (naturally or ecclesiastically):--sister.
8: of Hebrew origin (אֶבְיָתָר); Abiathar, an Israelite:--Abiathar.
80: from Α (as a connective particle) and (the womb); a brother (literally or figuratively) near or remote (much like Α):--brother.
81: from ἀδελφός; brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e. the (Christian) fraternity:--brethren, brotherhood.
82: from Α (as a negative particle) and δῆλος; hidden, figuratively, indistinct:--appear not, uncertain.
85: from a derivative of (to be sated to loathing); to be in distress (of mind):--be full of heaviness, be very heavy.
86: from Α (as negative particle) and εἴδω; properly, unseen, i.e. "Hades" or the place (state) of departed souls:--grave, hell.
87: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of διακρίνω; properly, undistinguished, i.e. (actively) impartial:--without partiality.
88: from Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of διά and λείπω; unintermitted, i.e. permanent:--without ceasing, continual.
89: adverb from ἀδιάλειπτος; uninterruptedly, i.e. without omission (on an appropriate occasion):--without ceasing.
9: of foreign origin (compare אָבֵל); Abilene, a region of Syria:--Abilene.
90: from a derivative of a compound of Α (as a negative particle) and a derivative of διαφθείρω; incorruptibleness, i.e. (figuratively) purity (of doctrine):--uncorruptness.
91: from ἄδικος; to be unjust, i.e. (actively) do wrong (morally, socially or physically):--hurt, injure, be an offender, be unjust, (do, suffer, take) wrong.
92: from ἀδικέω; a wrong done:--evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong.
93: from ἄδικος; (legal) injustice (properly, the quality, by implication, the act); morally, wrongfulness (of character, life or act):--iniquity, unjust, unrighteousness, wrong.
94: from Α (as a negative particle) and δίκη; unjust; by extension wicked; by implication, treacherous; specially, heathen:--unjust, unrighteous.
96: from Α (as a negative particle) and δόκιμος; unapproved, i.e. rejected; by implication, worthless (literally or morally):--castaway, rejected, reprobate.
97: from Α (as a negative particle); and δόλος; undeceitful, i.e. (figuratively) unadulterated:--sincere.
98: from (a place in Asia Minor); Adramyttene or belonging to Adramyttium:--of Adramyttium.
99: from (a place near its shore); the Adriatic sea (including the Ionian):--Adria.
